results.title: [Perf][Engram] Fuse head reordering with MXFP8 quantization
results.body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram shards embedding heads across TP ranks, but its replicated
`wkv` projection consumes token-major inputs. On the non-SP path, gathering along
`dim=1` reorders the rank-major collective output through a BF16 clone before
MXFP8 quantization. At 8192 tokens and width 6144, that intermediate is 96 MiB.

Gather once along `dim=0`, then fuse head reordering and padded-head removal into
MXFP8 quantization. The Triton kernel reads the gathered rank-major rows directly
and produces token-major FP8 values and F8_128x4 scales. `wkv` consumes the
`QuantizedActivation` directly, skipping its separate activation quantization.
There is still exactly one TP all-gather; the quantization helper performs no
communication.

The SP path already gathered along `dim=0` and used `_engram_select_rows` to
copy this rank's token window into a `T/tp`-sized BF16 buffer before
quantization. The same kernel takes `token_start` and `out_tokens`, so the SP
shard is quantized straight out of the gathered buffer as well; rows past the
last token quantize as zeros, exactly as the select kernel produced them.
Embedding lookup is unchanged under SP: every rank still looks up all `T`
tokens for its head shard, and only the projection and gate run on the shard.

Eligibility lives in the module-level `can_quantize_engram_gather`: TP>1 and a
`wkv` whose advertised input key is `kMxfp8Dynamic` on a FlashInfer CuTe-DSL or
CUTLASS MXFP8 kernel, because `QuantKey` does not encode the F8_128x4 scale
layout. The check goes through `get_input_quant_key`, so
consumers that require unquantized inputs fall back. Other configurations retain
their existing path. The kernel is launched with the PDL launch attribute as well
as the in-kernel `gdc_wait`/`gdc_launch_dependents`, matching the other Triton
kernels in the tree.

### Duplicate-work check

On 2026-09-15, searched open `vllm-project/vllm` PRs for `Engram`,
`MXFP8 gather`, and `Engram quantize`. No PR implementing this non-SP
reorder-plus-quantization fusion was found. Related
[#56435](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56435) changes SP redistribution
to all-to-all; [#56926](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56926) serializes
lookup streams, and [#56436](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56436)
controls lookup overlap. These address different operations. #56435 changes the
SP data layout, so whichever lands second must re-derive the SP window indexing
here. No issue number was provided for this change.

## Test Plan

Run from the repository with its CUDA-enabled `.venv` and FlashInfer CuTe-DSL
available. Both `.venv/bin` (for `ninja`) and the CUDA toolkit must be on `PATH`,
otherwise FlashInfer detection fails and the CUTLASS cases error instead of
skipping:

```bash
export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:/usr/local/cuda/bin:$PATH"
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py -q --disable-warnings --maxfail=1
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py -q \
  -k 'gather_quant or quantized_gather' --disable-warnings --maxfail=1
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/ops/engram_quant.py \
  tests/kernels/test_engram.py
git diff --check
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_engram_gather_quant.py
```

## Test Result

- Full Engram suite: **157 passed**, including a real two-GPU all-gather comparison.
- Focused tests: **73 passed, 84 deselected**.
- Bitwise equality of FP8 values and the complete scale buffer, including scale
  padding, across TP2/4/8 layouts, padded heads, zero tokens, decode and prefill
  shapes, the full token range plus first and last SP windows (including the
  zero-filled tail of the last shard), and CUDA Graph replay. Numerical tests cover every finite BF16 value
  in constant and mixed groups, signed zero, and very small/large inputs.
- Both real FlashInfer MXFP8 linear backends preserve bitwise-identical `wkv`
  outputs for non-SP and for SP ranks 1 and 3 of TP4, in eager execution, `torch.compile` with the eager backend, full CUDA
  Graph replay, and `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture` with the CPU-offload prefetch
  wait as a real eager break (one break, replay against refreshed rows). Tests
  reject accidental requantization of the fused input and check that
  `requires_unquantized_input` disables the fusion.
- Pre-commit and `git diff --check`: **passed**.

### Checkpoint projection validation

An additional local harness loaded actual `wkv` weights and scales from layers
1 and 14 of `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, revision
`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`. Both projections have weight shape
`[25600, 6144]`. With synthetic BF16 embedding rows and TP4 layouts, baseline and
fused CuTe-DSL projection outputs were bitwise identical at 1, 17, 128, and 8192
tokens: **8/8 comparisons passed**. This harness is not included in the PR.
Full-model generation, accuracy evaluation, and serving benchmarks were not run;
the fused path is bitwise identical to the existing quantization, so model output
is unchanged.

### Performance

Reproduced with `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_engram_gather_quant.py`.

One NVIDIA GB200; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132; FlashInfer 0.6.18; Triton 3.7.1; BF16
input, head dimension 256. Measurements use CUPTI, CUDA Graph replay, cold L2,
and the median sum of kernel times, with compilation and warmup excluded. The
benchmark starts from a simulated rank-major collective output and excludes
all-gather, embedding lookup, and GEMM. These are local operation timings, not
end-to-end speedups.

| TP | Heads | Tokens | Reorder + quantize (us) | Fused (us) | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 | 24 | 1 | 2.272 | 2.240 | 1.01x |
| 4 | 24 | 16 | 6.240 | 2.368 | 2.64x |
| 4 | 24 | 128 | 7.040 | 2.672 | 2.64x |
| 4 | 24 | 1024 | 23.072 | 5.600 | 4.12x |
| 4 | 24 | 8192 | 144.127 | 26.368 | 5.47x |
| 4 | 23 (padded) | 8192 | 247.136 | 26.368 | 9.37x |

For the 8192-by-6144 case, the net saving is **117.8 us (81.7%)** per Engram
layer per forward. The table was measured with the final kernel, including the
`token_start` / `out_tokens` window arguments; they are `do_not_specialize`
runtime scalars, and calling with eleven different (num_tokens, token_start,
out_tokens) combinations produced a single compiled variant. The kernel processes 128 MXFP8 groups per program with 4
warps, which measured about 2x faster than 32 groups at 1024 and 8192 tokens
and equal at decode sizes. At 8192 tokens it streams at about 5.6 TB/s, faster
than a plain PyTorch BF16-to-FP8 cast of the same bytes (29.8 us). At 1 to 16
tokens it is within 0.5 us of that cast and about 1 us above an empty launch,
so decode-size timings are launch-bound.

SP window, TP4, 24 heads, rank 1, same setup. Baseline is
`_engram_select_rows` plus FlashInfer quantization of the `T/tp` window:

| Tokens | Window | Select + quantize (us) | Fused (us) | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | 4 | 3.904 | 2.272 | 1.72x |
| 128 | 32 | 4.224 | 2.528 | 1.67x |
| 1024 | 256 | 7.776 | 3.328 | 2.34x |
| 8192 | 2048 | 29.120 | 9.056 | 3.22x |

Per Engram layer per forward this saves roughly 117 us (non-SP) or 20 us (SP)
at 8192 prefill tokens and 0 to 4 us at decode batch sizes, so end-to-end
throughput impact is small.

AI assistance was used for implementation, validation, and this PR description
(OpenAI Codex), and for review, kernel tile tuning, PDL launch wiring, and the
breakable-capture test. Human review of every changed line and
independent execution of relevant tests are required before submission.

results.title: [glm] [pcp] fuse norm rope with pcp cache gather
results.body:
## Summary

Fuse PCP Q/K preparation, cache quantization, and NVLS publication into one dispatch kernel plus one combine kernel for prefill, mixed, and decode batches.

* Old: bf16 norm/RoPE: output kv_c, k_pe, indexer_k → 3 all-gathers → quantize + cache-insertion 
* New: fused dispatch + NVLS multicast → local cache combine/scatter


### Dispatch

It launches one 256-thread CTA per local token and performs:

- Q RMSNorm, keeping Q local because each rank already holds the query rows it computes.
- KV RMSNorm.
- RoPE on `k_pe`.
- For sparse layers, indexer-K LayerNorm and RoPE.
- Packing directly into a cache-ready representation and NVLS multicast to every PCP rank.

For static E4M3, the fixed transport row is:

```text
| kv_c E4M3: 512 B | k_pe E4M3: 64 B | indexer K E4M3: 128 B | index scale FP32: 4 B | alignment: 12 B | = 720 B/token
```

For `fp8_ds_mla`, the fixed transport row is:

```text
| kv_c E4M3: 512 B | KV tile scales FP32: 16 B | k_pe BF16: 128 B | indexer K E4M3: 128 B | index scale FP32: 4 B | alignment: 12 B | = 800 B/token
```

Full workspace

```text
workspace[double_buffer_index][src rank][max_num_tokens][payload]
```

### Combine

The second kernel reads the received rank-major rows and scatters them into each rank's local paged caches:
- Prefill: tokens from every PCP rank are inserted.
- Decode: tokens are replicated, so they are inserted once from rank 0.

### Scope and limitations

- Requires CUDA and NVLS symmetric-memory multicast.
- Specialized for the GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek-V3.2 MLA dimensions above.
- Each rank retains a persistent double-buffered staging allocation of approximately `2 * num_ubatches * PCP_world_size * max_local_tokens * packed_row_bytes`.

## Performance

GLM-5.2 PCP8 on one 8×B300 node, TP1/PCP8/EP8, BF16 activations, static E4M3 KV cache, a 32K batched-token limit, and a 32K long-prefill threshold.

Default portable PCP pipeline (historical stage profile):

| Stage | Time |
| --- | ---: |
| Fused Q/K norm + K RoPE | 1.441 ms |
| Indexer-K all-gather | 2.064 ms |
| Indexer-K quantization/insertion | 0.423 ms |
| MLA `kv_c` all-gather | 11.044 ms |
| MLA `k_pe` all-gather | 2.349 ms |
| MLA quantization/insertion | 6.931 ms |
| **Total** | **24.252 ms** |

Final fused NVLS pipeline (latest two-run mean):

| Stage | Time |
| --- | ---: |
| Fused norm/RoPE + FP8 quantization + NVLS multicast | 8.228 ms |
| Cache combine/scatter | 0.898 ms |
| **Total** | **9.127 ms** |

Controlled current-stack full-forward A/B from the Kineto `execute_context_1(32768)_generation_0(0)` GPU annotation:

| Metric | Default portable PCP | Final fused NVLS | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mean across PCP ranks | 357.781 ms | 343.875 ms | **−3.89%** |
| Slowest PCP rank | 357.933 ms | 344.109 ms | **−3.86%** |

Each value is the arithmetic mean of two fresh-process runs. The portable baseline and pre-optimization fused path were measured in one current-stack ABBA; the final fused kernel was then measured in a second ABBA against that fused control. All runs used the same B300 node, model snapshot, source tree, eager-mode configuration, exact 32K input, warmup, and profiler procedure. The second ABBA measured the slowest-rank fused forward at 345.069 ms before these cache-overhead changes and 344.109 ms after them (−0.960 ms, −0.28%). "Default portable PCP" means the Triton fused norm/RoPE + PCP gather + cache-insert path.

## Relationship to existing work

- #52046 supplies the DeepSeek-V3.2 PCP gather-and-insert baseline now on `main`.
- #52839 moved the PCP attention helpers into `vllm/v1/attention/ops/pcp.py`; this branch is ported onto that layout.
- #52863 writes final rows directly into symmetric persistent cache replicas through P2P peer pointers.
- #49517 has the same replicated-KV-update goal using CUDA VMM peer mappings and direct peer stores.

This PR uses a different design from #52863/#49517: NVLS multicast into transient symmetric staging followed by a receiver-local paged-cache combine. It keeps cache tensors, allocation, and ownership ordinary and receiver-local, supports PCP2/4/8, and integrates with the common DeepSeek-V3.2 PCP path.

results.title: [Bugfix][XPU] Guard DeepSeek V4 CuTe DSL dispatch with CUDA platform
results.body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4-Flash on Intel XPU can select NVIDIA CuTe DSL kernels when CuTe DSL is installed. Three dispatch sites check `has_cutedsl()` without first checking the active platform.

This caused two successive startup failures on Stampede3 Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550:
- Indexer Q RoPE/quantization imported the NVIDIA implementation and failed because CUDA FlashAttention extensions were unavailable.
- After guarding that path, mixed prefill/decode warmup reached the CuTe DSL K-cache gather kernel and failed with `expected device_type=cuda`.

Require `current_platform.is_cuda()` before `has_cutedsl()` at the FP8 and MXFP4 indexer-Q dispatches and the K-cache dequantize/gather dispatch. Existing XPU kernels and the Triton fallback remain in use on non-CUDA platforms. CUDA selection is unchanged.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for `cutedsl xpu`, `"has_cutedsl" XPU`, and `"dequantize_and_gather_k_cache" "XPU"`.
Inspected #54460's patch: it skips XPU warmup and initializes indexer metadata; it does not fix these dispatch sites. This change fixes the runtime dispatch instead of skipping warmup. #41834 is broader NVIDIA SM12x enablement, not this targeted XPU fix.

## Test plan and results

- Human-reported hardware validation: after applying these three guards locally, DeepSeek-V4-Flash startup succeeded on Intel XPU, TP=8. The previously reported exceptions occurred before startup.
- Reproduction environment: vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev422+gd05da62e9.xpu`, `vllm-xpu-kernels==0.1.14.1`, PyTorch `2.13.0+xpu`, Triton `3.7.2+xpu`, Python 3.12.
- That environment also needed a separate local workaround for the MoE `topk_softplus_sqrt` 10/12-argument mismatch. That compatibility fix is proposed separately in #58049 and is **not** in this PR; startup success must not be attributed to these guards alone.
- Agent-side command: `.venv/bin/python review-vllm/check_dispatch.py`. An isolated temporary harness executed the changed functions extracted from source with mocked tensor allocation and kernel entrypoints: **18/18 dispatch cases passed** (CUDA/XPU/ROCm, CuTe DSL available/unavailable, FP8/MXFP4 indexer and cache gather). The same harness reproduced the three XPU dispatch failures against the original conditions. This is control-flow validation, not numerical or hardware testing; the temporary harness is not a repository test.
- Full repository pytest/pre-commit, CUDA numerical regression tests, generated-output correctness, and model evaluation have **not** been run. The exact rebased PR commit has not been run on XPU; hardware evidence is from the equivalent local edits on the version above.

## Draft status / AI assistance

Prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. The submitter applied the proposed local fixes and reported successful startup. Keep as draft pending review of the final diff and the outstanding repository/hardware tests; no inference accuracy or 1M-context validation is claimed.

results.title: [Perf] Vectorize DeepSeek V4.1 Triton K-cache gather
results.body:
Ports merged [Inferact/sra#77](https://github.com/Inferact/sra/pull/77) to `vllm-project/vllm:dsv41-feat` (base `c9d909e802a39292f54101bff8a36096761ea605`). Cherry-picked `fffe975387eba8c8de14b4e390ea3e35a0313bbe` without conflicts; the patch ID matches and both changed files are byte-identical to the source PR.

## Port validation

Run on this port:

```sh
/Users/daole/git/sra/.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/common/ops/cache_utils.py tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py
git diff --check upstream/dsv41-feat...HEAD
```

All applicable hooks and whitespace checks passed. GPU pytest, benchmarks, and model evaluations were not rerun for this port on the local macOS arm64 host. The GPU measurements below are the results reported by the original SRA PR, not new measurements against this branch.

Duplicate-work checks were refreshed: inspected the source PR and its comments, searched open SRA/upstream PRs by source URL and gather/vectorization keywords, and inspected all open PRs targeting `dsv41-feat`. No open PR implements this same V4.1 gather vectorization. The source PR is already merged into `sra-tracking`; this PR ports it to a different repository and target branch. No associated issue is being closed.

## Purpose

Vectorize the DeepSeek V4.1 Triton K-cache gather fallback. It currently expresses each token's seven FP8 quantization groups and BF16 tail as separate unrolled chunks. Load/dequantize/store the FP8 groups as one masked `[8, 64]` tile and copy the BF16 tail as one 64-element vector. The eighth FP8 row is masked, preserving the BF16 tail and excluding the padded scale byte.

The existing gather reference test now explicitly exercises the V4.1 Triton wrapper even when CuTeDSL is installed, and checks that output rows outside each gather window remain untouched.

Duplicate-work checks: searched open PRs in `Inferact/sra` and `vllm-project/vllm`. SRA #76 adds cache-format dispatch and sparse-index sentinel handling; it does not vectorize this kernel. Upstream [#49156](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49156) changes worker counts/warp configuration, and [#42504](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42504) adds a separate sparse-slot gather API. This change preserves the existing dense gather scheduling and interface. No associated issue is being closed.

## Original SRA test plan

Commands run:

```sh
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/common/ops/cache_utils.py tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py
git diff --check

# On gb200-rack1-05; standalone source copies bypass CuTeDSL dispatch.
cd /home/daole/benchmarks/dsv41-gather-bench.PQUxwZ
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH=/home/daole/benchmarks/dsv41-gather-bench.PQUxwZ/deps /home/daole/vllm-internal/.venv/bin/python -u bench.py --rounds 4 --iterations 100
```

The remote directory contains `bench.py`, verbatim baseline/candidate kernel and wrapper copies, `source_metadata.json` with source hashes, `change.diff`, `environment.json`, raw samples in `results.json`, and `REPORT.md`. The baseline is `0a5cb4e592a4a35a92f15b445cd3cc5340635f6e`. CUPTI dependencies were installed into that directory without modifying the existing environment.

Still to run in a full matching vLLM GPU environment:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py -k test_dequantize_and_gather_k_cache -v
```

## Original SRA test results

- All applicable pre-commit checks and whitespace checks passed.
- Both implementations exactly matched the independent PyTorch reference (`atol=rtol=0`) for 24 timed cases and four additional boundary cases. Coverage includes 64/128-token pages, shuffled physical pages, empty requests, partial gathers, output offsets, padded physical pages, the BF16 tail, and untouched output rows.
- On GPU 0 of `gb200-rack1-05` (NVIDIA GB200), the modified Triton kernel was **1.80–3.39x faster** across all 24 timed cases. Timings use CUPTI, CUDA graphs, cold L2, four alternating rounds of 100 samples, and the median of round medians. Setup, compilation, and cache flushing are outside kernel timing. Clocks were not locked; kernels were warmed before measurement, and no competing GPU workloads were observed.

Representative 64-token-page results:

| Requests x gathered tokens | Original us | Modified us | Speedup | Useful bandwidth, original -> modified GB/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 x 1 | 5.360 | 2.912 | 1.84x | 0.30 -> 0.55 |
| 1 x 512 | 17.496 | 6.528 | 2.68x | 47.0 -> 126.0 |
| 1 x 8192 | 217.457 | 66.305 | 3.28x | 60.5 -> 198.5 |
| 8 x 8192 | 240.825 | 71.240 | 3.38x | 437.3 -> 1478.3 |
| 32 x 2048 | 123.849 | 40.736 | 3.04x | 850.4 -> 2585.3 |

Environment: PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Triton 3.6.0, FlashInfer 0.6.13, CUPTI 13.4.0. Format: OCP FP8 E4M3 with UE8M0 scales and BF16 tail/output. Useful bandwidth assumes 1,607 bytes per gathered token (583 input/scale bytes + 1,024 output bytes), excluding metadata and transaction overhead; the peak measured case reached 2.62 TB/s with 128-token pages.

Limitations: the full repository pytest command and model evaluations have **not** been run. These are standalone kernel correctness/performance results, not serving throughput or accuracy results. FNUZ was excluded because the unchanged baseline cannot compile `fp8e4b8` on GB200 with this Triton version. CuTeDSL dispatch is unchanged, so these results only establish an improvement for the Triton fallback.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex implemented the change, extended the test, and ran the reported checks and benchmark. This is a draft for human review; the submitting human must review every changed line and run relevant tests before marking it ready.

results.title: [DeepSeek-V4][Preview][DO NOT MERGE] Batch-invariant kernels for 0-diff RL
results.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Preview only — DO NOT MERGE.**
>
> This draft collects the vLLM changes required for end-to-end DeepSeek-V4
> train/rollout alignment. It is intentionally larger than an upstreamable PR.
> After the preview is validated, it will be rebased onto current `main` and
> split by kernel, sparse attention, MoE/DeepEP, and reload support. Those
> focused PRs are the changes intended to merge. The verl production recipe
> will be updated after they land on official vLLM branches.

## Purpose

Make DeepSeek-V4 rollout execution independent of request batching so the same
vLLM kernels can be used by the mLite actor recomputation path and produce
exactly matching probabilities.

Preview source:

- head: `ISEEKYAN/vllm:ds4-v9-rc1`
- revision: `1a6542cdebbaabbf9972c358de8d6baa54e46b0c`
- tree: `df12131335d84e9848e188905449230902eaf7ca`
- fork point used by the image: `7aa248fcfef5ba7a6bfb0ce314e328ce63abb9f9`

Default vLLM behavior is unchanged. The aligned path is enabled only with
`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and the required native libraries.

### Fused activation and FP8 quantization

`csrc/batch_invariant/` adds a standalone
`fused_silu_mul_per_token_group_quant` operator for contiguous and
expert-masked inputs.

- Fuses SiLU, multiply, and 128-element group quantization with fixed launch
  geometry rather than selecting a path from batch-local M.
- Supports FP32, ceil-UE8M0, and packed UE8M0 scales.
- Uses architecture-specific activation/rounding behavior for Hopper and
  Blackwell.
- Uses 64-bit group and output offsets, including tensors above `2**31`
  elements.
- Is wired into `deep_gemm_moe.py` and `batched_deep_gemm_moe.py`.

In batch-invariant mode, missing kernel support is a hard error rather than a
silent fallback to a numerically different implementation.

### Deterministic sparse top-k

`csrc/ds4_bi_topk_extension.cu` adds `ds4_bi.top_k_per_row_prefill`.

- Selects top-k from a composite score/index key with a stable tie-break.
- Uses the same selector for prefill and batch-invariant decode.
- Canonicalizes selected indices before FlashMLA so reduction order is fixed.
- Keeps persistent row-start buffers for CUDA graph replay.

This removes top-k set/order changes caused by equal scores, request offsets,
or decode-versus-prefill dispatch.

### Sparse MLA and FlashMLA

`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py` and the sparse-attention helpers
add `VLLM_DS4_DECODE_KERNEL=sparse`.

- Decode gathers compressed and sliding-window KV and calls
  `flash_mla_sparse_fwd`, matching the prefill attention path.
- Batch-invariant prefill chunks each request independently instead of using a
  grouped batch-local plan.
- C128 top-k width, gather capacity, and workspaces derive from model capacity,
  not neighboring sequence lengths.
- Graph-safe Triton helpers fill top-k and length buffers without host sync.

This makes sparse index selection, KV gather order, and attention reduction
independent of the other requests in the batch.

### DeepGEMM, MoE, and DeepEP

- `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py` probes and enables the batch-invariant DeepGEMM
  contract, failing closed when the installed fork does not support it.
- MoE backend selection requires a batch-invariant implementation and uses a
  fixed expert capacity instead of `expert_num_tokens.max()`.
- Router gate logits use a common FP32 `torch.mm` path rather than an
  M-dependent low-latency GEMM.
- DeepEP low-latency dispatch is staged at fixed capacity; empty ranks still
  join collectives and FP8 dispatch requests aligned quantization.
- Shared experts launch once across staged dispatch slices.

Together these changes fix route ordering, expert input quantization, grouped
GEMM geometry, and combine order across actor and rollout.

### MHC, CUDA graphs, and weight reload

- Batch-invariant DeepSeek-V4 uses explicit MHC pre/post operations instead of
  the batch-dependent fused path.
- MHC split count is fixed and multi-token inputs are processed in stable
  token order.
- Sparse-attention, top-k, and MHC buffers keep stable addresses across CUDA
  graph capture and replay.
- Layerwise actor-to-rollout reload calls
  `finalize_weights_after_layerwise_reload()` to refresh MHC broadcast weights.
- `attn_sink` loading preserves `-inf` padding through the model weight loader.

### Hopper and Blackwell

- Hopper keeps FP32 block scales and uses the compatible block-scaled
  projection path in batch-invariant mode.
- Blackwell keeps packed UE8M0 scales and the DeepGEMM einsum path.
- Both architectures use their validated SiLU and FP8 packing behavior rather
  than treating SM90 and SM100+ as numerically interchangeable.

## Test Plan

- Run the batch-invariant kernel contract and large-tensor offset tests.
- Run deterministic sparse top-k tie/order tests.
- Run sparse FlashMLA and DeepSeek-V4 sparse decode tests.
- Run batch-invariant DeepGEMM/MoE and router gate tests.
- Run MHC graph/refit and layerwise reload tests.
- Load both custom libraries on x86_64 and arm64 images.
- Run the companion verl `quick_alignment_test`, H100 aligned profile, and
  GB200 aligned profile.

results.title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Keep FP8 Engram rows packed through TP exchange
results.body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram's CPU/UVA lookup currently expands checkpoint FP8 values and UE8M0 scales into BF16 before the TP head all-gather. This opt-in change stages each selected head as FP8 value bytes followed by its original scale bytes, exchanges one `uint8` payload, then reconstructs the existing BF16 tensor once before `wkv`. At head dimension 256 and 32-value scale blocks, the TP payload is 264 instead of 512 bytes per head row; this is a byte-count reduction, not a measured serving speedup. The original BF16 lookup and exchange remain the fallback for small batches and unsupported configurations.

Enable it with `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"packed_fp8_exchange":true,"packed_fp8_exchange_min_tokens":256}'`. The initial path requires effective Engram-DP size 1, TP>1, non-SP execution, no microbatching/PCP/DCP, and a head dimension divisible by the scale block size. The token threshold is a conservative policy knob pending target-hardware crossover measurements. Persistent packed staging keeps the asynchronous UVA lookup's addresses stable; all TP ranks select the same representation from the batch shape, and the post-exchange dequantization uses the same FP8-to-FP32, UE8M0 exponent and BF16 rounding sequence as the current lookup. `wkv` and the public Engram output contract are unchanged.

This does not duplicate #56929, which begins with a BF16 collective result and fuses head reordering with WKV activation quantization, or #56435, which changes SP redistribution to all-to-all. #56512 supplies the existing CPU/UVA prefetch that this path reuses. If those PRs land, the non-SP transport boundary and end-to-end crossover must be remeasured on the rebased head.

results.title: [AMD][DSV4.1Flash] Quantize MoE activations to MXFP8 before the MoRI dispatch
results.body:
## Motivation

MXFP4 W4A16 experts declare BF16 activations, so MoRI dispatches raw BF16 and
AITER quantizes to group-32 MXFP8 on arrival. A token routed to `k` distinct
ranks is therefore quantized `k` times — expected ~4.4 of 8 ranks at topk=6 for
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash — and the dispatch carries 2 bytes/element instead of
1 + 1/32.

Quantizing in `prepare()` moves that to once per token on the rank that owns it,
and roughly halves the dispatch payload.

AITER already consumes the result: with a pre-quantized FP8 operand and E8M0
scales, its stage-1 path sorts the scales (`mxfp4_moe_sort_fwd`) instead of
running its own quant. This mirrors the MXFP4 W4A4 dispatch added in #59596,
which takes the same pre-quantized route for a4w4.

## Summary of changes

**`all2all_utils.py`** — adds `mori_use_mxfp8_dispatch()` and wires a third
dispatch mode into `maybe_make_prepare_finalize()`. MoRI infers the payload
dtype from the input tensor and transports `scale_dim` scales of
`scale_type_size` bytes per token, so the new branch sets
`scale_dim = hidden_dim / 32` and a 1-byte scale element. E8M0 exponents are
bytes, not the fp32 the per-token/per-tensor FP8 paths use.

**`prepare_finalize/mori.py`** — adds the `use_mxfp8_dispatch` flag and the
corresponding quant in `prepare()`, via `get_hip_quant(QuantType.per_1x32)` with
`scale_type=dtypes.fp8_e8m0`, matching the FP4 branch directly above it. The
mutual-exclusion assert becomes `sum(...) <= 1` now that there are three modes.

**Gating is deliberately narrow.** A pre-quantized operand is only safe when
AITER would have produced MXFP8 itself: a BF16-activation kernel would cast the
FP8 payload back to BF16 and never apply the scales, silently losing the
scaling. `mori_use_mxfp8_dispatch()` therefore asks AITER directly via
`resolve_activation_dtype()`, which is documented for exactly this case ("lets a
caller that produces the activations itself -- an all-to-all dispatch, a fused
epilogue -- emit that dtype directly") and returns `None` rather than guessing
when the answer would have depended on a token count that does not exist yet.
It also fails closed on `ImportError` and on a hidden dim that is not a multiple
of 32.

## Results

8x MI355X (gfx950), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DP8/EP8 with `mori_high_throughput`,
speculative decoding off. 8192 in / 1024 out, 256 prompts at concurrency 64,
against a stock nightly (`0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82`) with **only this change
applied** — this PR was measured on its own, with no AITER-side patches, so the
numbers are attributable to the dispatch change alone.

Engagement was confirmed rather than assumed: `resolve_activation_dtype(M=None)`
returns `torch.float8_e4m3fn` under the `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0` that vLLM
pins for this model, and the dispatch kernel switches from
`EpDispatchIntraNodeKernel_bf16` to `EpDispatchIntraNodeKernel_fp8_ocp`.

### Performance

| Metric | Baseline | With patch | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 1103.58 | 1309.33 | **+18.6%** |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 9932.18 | 11783.95 | **+18.6%** |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 54.16 | 46.83 | **-13.5%** |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 54.68 | 46.69 | **-14.6%** |
| Median ITL (ms) | 51.40 | 44.29 | -13.8% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 3392.14 | 2248.40 | -33.7% |
| Benchmark duration (s) | 237.54 | 200.21 | -15.7% |

### Accuracy

gsm8k, 5-shot, all 1319 questions.

| Arm | strict-match | stderr | Delta | flexible-extract |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 0.9196 | 0.0075 | — | 0.9196 |
| With patch | 0.9280 | 0.0071 | +0.0084 | 0.9287 |

Within ~1 sigma of baseline. The same mxfp8 quantization is applied either way;
this only changes which rank performs it and how many times.

### Reproduction

Server:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1
export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1

vllm serve /model/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput \
  --moe-backend aiter \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --language-model-only \
  --no-swa-bounded-replay \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}'
```

Benchmark:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tokenizer /model/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 1024 \
  --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 256 \
  --max-concurrency 64 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --seed 0 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \
  --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

Accuracy:

```bash

  --model_args base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,tokenizer_backend=None,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,timeout=3600
```

results.title: [Quantization] Remove the dead ocp_mx_scheme branch from moe_kernel_quantize_input
results.body:
## Purpose

Shortly, remove dead code.

`moe_kernel_quantize_input()` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/utils.py` carries an `ocp_mx_scheme: str | None = None` parameter and opens its body with a block that short-circuits `*_a_fp8` OCP MX schemes into `_fp8_quantize_dequantize` before the normal `quant_dtype` dispatch ever runs. Nothing reaches that block. This PR removes the parameter and the block.

This is the follow-up @fxmarty-amd asked for when introduced the `quantization_emulation` path that superseded the block, in #46142 (`e368415daa`):

> [r3452957212](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46142/files#r3452957212):
> "Yes I don't think this code block is needed"
> [r3453008225](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46142/files#r3453008225):
> "Let's address in an other PR."

This is the left TODO:

```python
# TODO: Remove this `ocp_mx_scheme is not None` block and rely solely
# on `quantization_emulation`.
```

and reconfirmed the ask in review on #43983 ([review 4904664996](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43983#pullrequestreview-4904664996)), linking `utils.py#L288-L301` — exactly the lines removed here.

### Why deleting it changes no behavior

The only arm with behavior was `.endswith("a_fp8")`, and the only **reachable** a_fp8 scheme is `w_mxfp4_a_fp8` — `w_mxfp6_e3m2_a_fp8` and `w_mxfp6_e2m3_a_fp8`, both raise `NotImplementedError` earlier, in `QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod.get_fused_moe_quant_config`.

For `w_mxfp4_a_fp8` the two paths are identical:

|  | deleted arm | surviving dispatch |
|---|---|---|
| condition | `ocp_mx_scheme.endswith("a_fp8")` | `quant_dtype == current_platform.fp8_dtype()` and `quantization_emulation` |
| action | `return _fp8_quantize_dequantize(A, A_scale)` | `return _fp8_quantize_dequantize(A, A_scale)` |

`_fp8_quantize_dequantize` takes only `A` and `A_scale`, so nothing else was being bypassed. `OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts.__init__` sets both inputs (`quantization_emulation = True`, `_quant_dtype = current_platform.fp8_dtype()`), and `TritonExperts.apply` forwards them.

results.title: [Bugfix][MoE] Size the FlashInfer one-sided dispatch for experts that quantize their own inputs
results.body:
## Purpose

With a block-FP8 MoE, `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass` and `--all2all-backend flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`, `FlashInferExperts.expects_unquantized_inputs` is True, so the one-sided prepare step dispatches the BF16 activations and the CUTLASS kernel quantizes them itself. `make_fp8_moe_kernel` builds the prepare/finalize before the experts and passes no `input_dtype`, so `flashinfer_one_sided_dispatch_layout` sizes the MoeAlltoAll workspace for FP8 rows plus FP32 1x128 scales. For hidden size 2560 and top-k 10 that is 2,720 bytes per token (2560 + 80 + 80 for top-k ids and weights) where 5,200 are dispatched.

FlashInfer lays out the dispatch payloads from the actual tensor sizes of each call, puts the combine region right after them, and checks both against the per-rank workspace size. An undersized workspace therefore works until a step's largest per-rank token count gets close to the size the workspace was reserved for (`max_num_batched_tokens`), and then combine raises `workspace insufficient for combine payload region`. For the shapes above that happens at about 76% of `max_num_batched_tokens`. On main this makes the configuration below fail at startup: the profile run dispatches `max_num_batched_tokens` tokens on every rank and combine raises that error, so the engine never comes up.

This PR:

- `make_fp8_moe_kernel` builds standard-format experts before the prepare/finalize (they do not depend on it) and passes `input_dtype=moe_config.in_dtype` when `experts.expects_unquantized_inputs`, the same way #57176 sizes the dispatch for per-token NVFP4. Batched-format experts are still built after the prepare/finalize, from its max tokens and dispatcher count.
- `make_eep_staged_quant_method`, which rebuilds the prepare/finalize for elastic EP, passes `input_dtype` from the existing experts' `expects_unquantized_inputs`. It passed none before, so the rebuild also dropped the per-token NVFP4 sizing from #57176.

Experts that quantize before the dispatch (DeepGEMM, Triton without LoRA) keep the FP8 + scales layout.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs for `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`, `one-sided dispatch`, `one_sided_dispatch_layout`, `expects_unquantized_inputs`, `defer_input_quant all2all`, `combinePayloadOffset` and `workspace insufficient for combine`. #57176 (merged) fixed the same sizing for per-token NVFP4 only. #57073 adds a new all-to-all backend that reuses `flashinfer_one_sided_dispatch_layout`, #50030 changes FP8 backend selection only, and #49335 fixes MXFP8 scale swizzling after the dispatch; none of them changes how the FP8 dispatch is sized.

**Not covered:** `TritonExperts` defers input quantization only once a MoE LoRA context is attached, which happens after the kernel is built, so FP8 MoE LoRA with the one-sided dispatch still reserves FP8 rows.

## Test Plan

8x H20 (96 GB), CUDA 13.3, torch 2.13.0, FlashInfer 0.7.0 (the pinned version).

```bash
# New unit tests: the FP8 oracle requests a BF16 dispatch layout for FlashInferExperts
# and keeps FP8 + scales for TritonExperts; the elastic EP rebuild passes input_dtype
# from the existing experts. They fail on main for the two buggy cases.
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py -k "one_sided_dispatch_sized or eep_rebuild"

# Existing tests around the change
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py
pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -k one_sided
pytest tests/distributed/test_mnnvl_alltoall.py -k one_sided   # 2 GPUs

# Real MoeAlltoAll on 2 GPUs (script below): workspace sized with main's block-FP8 layout
# vs. the BF16 layout, BF16 dispatch + identity-expert combine at 25-100% of max tokens
python repro_undersized_layout.py --layout fp8
python repro_undersized_layout.py --layout bf16

# End to end, main vs. this PR: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (block FP8, hidden 2560, 512 experts,
# top-10), DP=4 / EP=4 on 4x H20, flashinfer_cutlass + flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided,
# --max-num-batched-tokens 16384. Then 48 concurrent 19k-token prompts (full 16384-token
# prefill steps on every DP rank) and GSM8K (1319 questions, 0-shot chat, thinking off, greedy).
```

## Test Result

- New tests: 4 passed. On main, `[flashinfer_cutlass]` and `[True]` (elastic EP) fail with `assert None == torch.bfloat16`; the other two pass.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py`: 33 passed, 18 skipped (SM100-only cases). `test_online.py -k one_sided`: 8 passed. `test_mnnvl_alltoall.py -k one_sided`: 2 passed, 3 skipped (no `SYS_PTRACE` in this container).
- `pre-commit` passes.

Real `MoeAlltoAll`, 2 ranks, hidden 2560, top-10, 64 experts, `max_num_tokens` 4096:

| tokens per rank | main's layout (64.9 MB per rank) | BF16 layout (85.3 MB per rank) |
|---:|---|---|
| 1024-3072 (25-75%) | correct | correct |
| 3276 (80%) | `RuntimeError: workspace insufficient for combine payload region` | correct |
| 4096 (100%) | (not reached) | correct |

"Correct" means every rank received exactly the tokens routed to it, intact, and combine returned `x * (number of distinct destination ranks)` for every token.

End to end, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, DP=4 / EP=4 on 4x H20, `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass --all2all-backend flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided --max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, everything else default:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| startup | fails in `profile_run` (below) | ok |
| 48 concurrent 19,429-token prompts (full 16,384-token prefill steps on every DP rank) | — | 48/48 succeeded, no errors in the server log |
| GSM8K, 1319 questions, 0-shot chat, thinking off, greedy | — | 0.960 (0 invalid) |

On main every rank's profile-run dispatch was 16,384 BF16 rows (`a1=(16384, 2560)`, `defer_input_quant=True`) into a workspace sized for FP8 rows (516,686,208 bytes per rank):

```text
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 626, in determine_available_memory
  self.model_runner.profile_run()
...
File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided.py", line 176, in finalize
File ".../vllm/distributed/device_communicators/all2all.py", line 873, in combine_into
File ".../flashinfer/comm/trtllm_moe_alltoall.py", line 266, in moe_a2a_combine_into
RuntimeError: Check failed: (combinePayloadOffset >= 0 && combinePayloadOffset + payloadBytes <= sizePerRank) is false: workspace insufficient for combine payload region
```

For comparison, our production build (an older vLLM in which this dispatch is hard-coded to BF16) scores 0.958 with the same client.

- AI assistance: this PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude, via Cursor), including the fix, tests and the reproduction. The commit carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer. I have reviewed every changed line.

<details>
<summary>repro_undersized_layout.py</summary>

```python
"""Reproduce what happens when the FlashInfer one-sided workspace is sized for block-FP8
dispatch (hidden bytes + fp32 1x128 scales) but BF16 activations are dispatched, as with
FLASHINFER_CUTLASS block-FP8 experts (expects_unquantized_inputs=True).

    python repro_undersized_layout.py [--layout fp8|bf16] [--world-size 2]

Every row a rank dispatches encodes (source rank, token index) in small integers that are
exact in BF16. Each rank checks that it received exactly the tokens routed to it, intact,
then combines with identity experts and checks every token comes back as
x * (number of distinct destination ranks).
"""

import argparse
import os
import traceback

import torch
import torch.multiprocessing as mp

HIDDEN, TOP_K, NUM_EXPERTS, MAX_TOKENS = 2560, 10, 64, 4096
FRACTIONS = (0.25, 0.5, 0.7, 0.75, 0.8, 1.0)


def make_inputs(src, t):
    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(1000 * src + t)
    topk_ids = torch.rand(t, NUM_EXPERTS, device="cuda", generator=g).topk(TOP_K, dim=1)
    topk_ids = topk_ids.indices.to(torch.int32)
    topk_w = torch.rand(t, TOP_K, device="cuda", generator=g)
    tok = torch.arange(t, device="cuda")
    x = (torch.arange(HIDDEN, device="cuda") % 7 + 1).repeat(t, 1).float()
    x[:, 0] = src + 1
    x[:, 1] = tok // 128
    x[:, 2] = tok % 128
    return x.to(torch.bfloat16).contiguous(), topk_ids, topk_w


def worker(rank, world_size, port, dp_port, layout, queue):
    try:
        os.environ.pop("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES", None)
        torch.accelerator.set_device_index(rank)
        from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
        from vllm.config.parallel import ParallelConfig
        from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import (
            ensure_model_parallel_initialized,
            get_dp_group,
            init_distributed_environment,
        )

        cfg = VllmConfig()
        cfg.parallel_config = ParallelConfig(
            data_parallel_size=world_size,
            data_parallel_rank=rank,
            _data_parallel_master_port_list=[int(dp_port)],
        )
        with set_current_vllm_config(cfg):
            init_distributed_environment(
                world_size=1, rank=0, distributed_init_method=f"tcp://localhost:{port}",
                local_rank=rank,
            )
            ensure_model_parallel_initialized(1, 1)

        from vllm.distributed.device_communicators.all2all import (
            FlashInferNVLinkOneSidedManager,
        )

        manager = FlashInferNVLinkOneSidedManager(get_dp_group().cpu_group)
        if layout == "fp8":  # what vLLM main computes for block FP8
            x_bytes, sf_bytes = HIDDEN, HIDDEN // 128 * 4
        else:  # what is actually dispatched
            x_bytes, sf_bytes = HIDDEN * 2, 0
        manager.initialize(
            max_num_tokens=MAX_TOKENS, top_k=TOP_K, num_experts=NUM_EXPERTS,
            hidden_size=HIDDEN, x_bytes_per_token=x_bytes, x_sf_bytes_per_token=sf_bytes,
        )
        a2a = manager.moe_alltoall
        per_rank = NUM_EXPERTS // world_size
        pattern = (torch.arange(HIDDEN, device="cuda") % 7 + 1).float()
        results = []
        for frac in FRACTIONS:
            t = int(MAX_TOKENS * frac)
            x, topk_ids, topk_w = make_inputs(rank, t)
            try:
                recv_x, recv_ids, _ = a2a.dispatch(
                    token_selected_experts=topk_ids, input_payloads=[x, topk_ids, topk_w],
                    runtime_max_tokens_per_rank=t, invalid_token_expert_id=-1,
                    expert_id_payload_index=1,
                )
                torch.accelerator.synchronize()
                recv_x = recv_x.view(world_size, t, HIDDEN).float()
                recv_ids = recv_ids.view(world_size, t, TOP_K)
                bad = 0
                for src in range(world_size):
                    _, src_ids, _ = make_inputs(src, t)
                    want = torch.nonzero((src_ids // per_rank == rank).any(-1)).flatten()
                    rows = recv_x[src][(recv_ids[src] // per_rank == rank).any(-1)]
                    got = (rows[:, 1] * 128 + rows[:, 2]).long()
                    bad += int((rows[:, 0] != src + 1).sum())
                    bad += int((rows[:, 3:] != pattern[3:]).any(-1).sum())
                    bad += int(got.numel() != want.numel() or
                               not torch.equal(got.sort().values, want))
                manager.combine_into(
                    payload=recv_x.to(torch.bfloat16).contiguous(),
                    runtime_max_tokens_per_rank=t, output=(out := torch.empty_like(x)),
                )
                torch.accelerator.synchronize()
                n_dst = sum((topk_ids // per_rank == r).any(-1).int() for r in range(world_size))
                bad_out = int((out.float() != x.float() * n_dst[:, None]).any(-1).sum())
                status = f"dispatch errors={bad}, wrong combined tokens={bad_out}/{t}"
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                status = f"EXCEPTION {type(e).__name__}: {str(e).splitlines()[0][:160]}"
            results.append((frac, t, status))
            torch.distributed.barrier(group=get_dp_group().cpu_group)
            if status.startswith("EXCEPTION"):
                break
        queue.put((rank, manager.workspace_size, results))
        manager.cleanup()
    except Exception:
        queue.put((rank, None, traceback.format_exc()))


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--layout", choices=["fp8", "bf16"], default="fp8")
    p.add_argument("--world-size", type=int, default=2)
    a = p.parse_args()
    from vllm.utils.network_utils import get_open_port

    mp.set_start_method("spawn")
    port, dp_port = str(get_open_port()), str(get_open_port())
    q = mp.Queue()
    procs = [mp.Process(target=worker, args=(r, a.world_size, port, dp_port, a.layout, q))
             for r in range(a.world_size)]
    for pr in procs:
        pr.start()
    outs = [q.get(timeout=900) for _ in procs]
    for pr in procs:
        pr.join(timeout=60)
    for rank, ws, res in sorted(outs, key=lambda o: o[0]):
        print(f"== layout={a.layout} rank {rank} workspace_size_per_rank={ws}")
```

results.title: [ROCm] Fuse RMSNorm into MXFP8 activation quant on CDNA4
results.body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash quantizes every dense-linear activation to MXFP8 in a standalone kernel launch immediately before the `tl.dot_scaled` GEMM. Profiling a decode step on MI355X (gfx950) shows **187–198 of these quant/GEMM pairs per step, adjacent 100% of the time**, and the producer feeding the quant is almost always AITER's `add_rmsnorm`.

AITER's `add_rmsnorm_quant` / `rmsnorm_quant` already emit exactly the `(FP8 E4M3 value, per-32 E8M0 uint8 scale)` pair that `dot_scaled` consumes. So the quant launch can be **deleted outright** rather than merely made cheaper — no new kernel, no redundant work.

This PR adds the two custom ops plus the `torch.compile` patterns that rewrite

```
(fused_add_)rms_norm -> mxfp8_quantize
```

into the single fused AITER kernel.

## Why not fuse into the GEMM prologue

The obvious alternative — quantize in-register in the GEMM prologue — was implemented and measured first, and **rejected**: it came in at **0.28–0.89x** versus baseline. Triton's lowering of the reshape+reduce on gfx950 adds ~26 µs to a 12 µs GEMM in order to save a 4.4 µs launch. Producer-side fusion avoids that entirely because the norm already has the values resident.

## Results

Measured on the norm+quant pair at hidden 5120, amortizing over 64 copies per graph replay to get above the ~11 µs graph-dispatch floor:

| | latency | speedup |
|---|---|---|
| `add_rmsnorm` + separate MXFP8 quant | baseline | 1.00x |
| `add_rmsnorm_quant` (fused) | 2.2–4.1 µs saved per occurrence | **1.49–1.77x** |

At ~190 occurrences per decode step this is ~1% of step time.

## Dependency

**Requires https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5480** (merged). Without it, `add_rmsnorm_quant` aborts with `group_size not support: 32` for hidden sizes in `(4096, 6144]`, because those map to `thread_data_size=24` and `32 % 24 != 0` — and 5120 is exactly this model's hidden size. That PR extends the dispatch to route non-multiples of 24 in that band to the `(512,16)`/`(1024,8)` configs, mirroring logic the `n <= 8192` branch already had.

Gating is capability-based (`is_mxfp8_norm_fusion_enabled()` = aiter enabled + `supports_mx()`), with no new env var, since this is strictly a win wherever it applies. On non-CDNA4 the MXFP8 linear falls through to BF16 emulation and never emits a quant op to fuse with, so the patterns are not registered there.

## Test Plan

`tests/compile/passes/test_aiter_rms_mxfp8_quant_fusion.py` covers three graph shapes:

- `rms_norm -> mxfp8_quantize`
- `fused_add_rms_norm -> mxfp8_quantize` (the shape that dominates the decode step)
- the same with the 2D flatten that `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel.apply_weights` inserts

Each asserts the pass matched exactly once, that the fused op is present after the pass, and that `mxfp8_quantize` is **fully** eliminated (`check_before_ops`).

On numerics: AITER and vLLM break ties differently when rounding a block amax to its E8M0 scale, so a few blocks per thousand land one power of two apart and no elementwise tolerance holds. The test instead asserts the fused kernel is **no less faithful** than the quant it replaces, comparing both against an fp32 reference of the same math (fused 0.0224 vs unfused 0.0225 relative L1; fused is marginally better). The residual output is bit-exact.

## Test Result

```
tests/compile/passes/test_aiter_rms_mxfp8_quant_fusion.py ... 3 passed
tests/compile/passes/test_double_aiter_rms_quant_fusion.py .. 3 passed, 2 skipped
```

Also verified on the real graph — vLLM's own `RMSNorm` module plus the actual `_mxfp8_dot_scaled_linear`, compiled through the full `PostGradPassManager` rather than the fusion pass alone:

```
mxfp8_quantize   before=1 after=0
fused norm+quant before=0 after=1
GEMM output rel_l1 fused vs unfused: 0.01702
residual bitexact: True
```

Context: this is item 7.2 of RFC #56506.

results.title: [Superseded] [Quark] Cache dequantized MXFP4 fallback weights
[Feature][Spec-Decode]: Cascade: Utility-Driven Adaptive k for MoE Speculative Decoding in V1
results.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Status Quo
In `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`, `num_spec_tokens` is set once at engine init and never changes:

```python
self.num_spec_tokens = speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens
if speculative_config.use_eagle():
    self.use_eagle = True
    self.num_lookahead_tokens = self.num_spec_tokens  # fixed for lifetime of engine
```
`num_lookahead_tokens` flows into `kv_cache_manager.allocate_slots()` which pre-allocates KV slots assuming every request in every batch will use exactly `k` draft tokens. Today, there exists no mechanism to vary `k` per-request or disable speculation for a specific request mid-flight without restarting the engine.

This is fine for dense models, however, **for MoE it is actively harmful**. On a dense model, verification overhead is roughly constant because the target model reads all weights regardless of how many draft tokens it verifies. On the other hand, on MoE, every additional draft token activates a different expert subset, so verification data movement scales with `k`, not batch size.  At typical math or reasoning acceptance rates, this makes speculation a net loss.  Cascade (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20675) quantifies this precisely across five MoE models.

In `vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py`, `propose()` has no per-request state. There is nowhere to track acceptance history, utility, or current `k` per request — the entire batch gets the same `num_spec_tokens`.

## Proposed Solution
Upstream [**Cascade** (MLSys 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20675) to vLLM V1. Cascade introduces per-request **speculation utility**:
 
```
utility = tokens_accepted / verification_cost(k)
```

Two phases per request — short **test** phase probes k=1..K_max, long **set** phase locks the utility-maximizing K*. If utility < 1.0, speculation is disabled for that request without evicting the draft model.

Paper results on H100: worst-case slowdown **54% → 5%**, throughput improvement **7–14%** over static k.

## What changes in V1
Three components need to change: 
- `per-request state` tracking in the proposer,
- `per-request slot allocation` in the scheduler, and 
- `variable-length draft` handling in the model runner

For CUDA graphs, draft inputs will be padded to `K_max` with masked unused positions, consistent with how existing spec-decode graph captures handle variable batch sizes in `gpu_model_runner.py`.

#### Validation target: NVIDIA B200 (Blackwell)

cc @benchislett 

### Alternatives

Static k tuning reduces but does not eliminate the problem, optimal k varies per request and per task. Prior work #26504 explored `acceptance-rate-based dynamic k` but that does not account for expert activation overhead, which is the dominant cost on MoE verification. 

### Additional context

- Cascade paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20675
- MLSys 2026 poster: https://mlsys.org/virtual/2026/poster/10189
- Prior variable-k PR: #26504
- Spec-decode tracking issue: #28947
- Q2 2026 roadmap: #39749

results.title: [ROCm][Perf] FP8 o-projection for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash MLA on AMD MI355X
results.body:
## FP8 o-projection for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash MLA on AMD MI355X

Ports the FP8 output-projection chain (`wo_a`) from the CUDA path to ROCm
on MI355X (gfx950). CUDA already runs `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`; ROCm was
dequantizing the FP8 E4M3 `wo_a` weight to BF16 and running `torch.einsum`
on every forward pass of all 40 layers.

### What changes

**`vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/amd/rocm.py`**

- `rocm_prepare_inv_rope_woa_fp8` / `prepare_wo_a_fp8`: new load-time hook
  that rearranges the checkpoint's 32×32 E8M0 block scales to the 128×128
  layout expected by `batched_gemm_a8w8_mxscale`, storing the result and a
  pre-computed FP32 cos/sin cache on the layer.
- `DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention.forward`: FP8 fast path using
  `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` (Triton) → `batched_gemm_a8w8_mxscale`
  (AITER CK), with fallback to the existing BF16 path when
  `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` and the cache is cold.

**Why load-time, not lazy:**
Decode at this serving configuration dispatches `CUDAGraphMode.FULL`. A cold
cos/sin cache at CUDA-graph capture time permanently bakes the BF16 fallback
into every replay for the lifetime of the process. The preparation therefore
runs in `process_weights_after_loading`; V4.1 reaches this hook twice (once
pre-quant-finalize), so the prime uses a sticky-retry/recompute guard.

### Correctness

Scale rearrangement (32×32 → 128×128 E8M0) measures **164.7 dB** against the
exact fp32 dequant — the same tensor. End-to-end SNR **31.4–31.6 dB** equals
the producer-alone SNR at every M (1, 6, 192, 4096), confirming that all
precision loss is FP8 activation quantization — identical to what CUDA's
`deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` performs, not introduced by the scale rearrangement.
Output is bitwise-identical to the BF16 path within FP8 tolerance at every
measured shape.

### Component-level speedup (MI355X gfx950, graph-captured, weakest-of-5)

| Batch M | Serving context | `wo_a` kernel: BF16 → FP8 |
|--------:|----------------|--------------------------|
| 1 | decode / TPOT | **1.51×** |
| 6 | DSpark verify block | **1.17×** |
| 192 | C32 operating point (25.73 µs → 18.85 µs) | **1.53×** |
| 4096 | prefill / TTFT | **1.38×** |

Speedup fades toward large M as expected for a weight-bandwidth-bound kernel.

### End-to-end benchmark (MI355X, TP=4, C=32, agentic-coding scenario)

| Metric | Before | After | Δ |
|--------|-------:|------:|--:|
| Output throughput | 231.76 tok/s/chip | 244.33 tok/s/chip | **+5.42%** |
| p90 interactivity | 33.77 tok/s/user | 36.97 tok/s/user | **+9.48%** |
| p90 TPOT | 29.6 ms | 27.1 ms | **−8.5%** |

~5.8σ above the measured cross-run coefficient of variation (0.94%).

results.title: [Bug]:  FlashInfer B12x W4A16 runtime repacking retains original and packed MoE weights, causing startup OOM
results.body:
### Your current environment


## Your current environment

```text
GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (31.36 GiB, SM120)
NVIDIA driver: 580.126.18
vLLM: 0.25.1
FlashInfer: 0.6.13
PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130
CUDA toolkit: 13.0.2
Transformers: 5.10.1
compressed-tensors: 0.17.0
vLLM source revision inspected: c71a583aa9f81400528e67e3d818f66b804e8340
Model: private Qwen3.6-35B-A3B derivative
Weight/activation mode: W4A16 (NVFP4 weights, BF16 activations)
KV cache dtype: FP8
Checkpoint size: 23,349,927,384 bytes
```

Relevant checkpoint metadata (the model name and weights are private, but the architecture and quantization contract are not):

```text
architecture: Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration
model_type: qwen3_5_moe
hidden_size: 2048
num_hidden_layers: 40
num_experts: 256
num_experts_per_tok: 8
moe_intermediate_size: 512
quant_method: compressed-tensors
format: nvfp4-pack-quantized
weight bits/type: 4-bit float
weight group_size: 16
input_activations: null (W4A16/BF16 activations)
weight scale dtype: torch.float8_e4m3fn
KV cache: 8-bit float, per-tensor symmetric
```


### 🐛 Describe the bug



The FlashInfer B12x W4A16 path performs an additional GPU-side weight repack on the first MoE invocation after vLLM has loaded the complete checkpoint. The repacked weights are retained in FlashInfer's process-global
`_W4A16_WEIGHT_CACHE`, while vLLM's `RoutedExperts` continues to own the source `w13_weight`, `w2_weight`, and scale parameters.

For a model that fits tightly on a 32 GiB SM120 GPU with its original NVFP4 checkpoint layout, the additional persistent packed copies and the temporary repacking tensors make the B12x backend fail during startup/warmup. Marlin can load the same W4A16 checkpoint because it does not take this B12x preparation
path.

This is not only a transient allocator peak. FlashInfer creates full repacked copies of both expert matrices and keeps them strongly referenced for the process lifetime:

```python
# flashinfer/.../blackwell_sm12x/moe_dispatch.py
_W4A16_WEIGHT_CACHE: Dict[Tuple, W4A16PackedWeights] = {}

prepared = prepare_w4a16_packed_weights(...)
_W4A16_WEIGHT_CACHE[key] = prepared
```

`W4A16PackedWeights` contains `w13`, `w2`, both block-scale tensors, both
global-scale tensors, and a workspace. `prepare_w4a16_packed_weights()` creates
`packed_w13` and `packed_w2` with `_repack_weight()` and returns them in that
object. There is no cache clear/eviction path.

On the vLLM side, `RoutedExperts` explicitly owns the original expert
parameters. `FlashInferB12xExperts.apply()` passes those original tensors to
`B12xMoEWrapper.run()` on every call. The integration neither replaces nor
releases the original parameters after FlashInfer prepares its packed layout.

### Reproduction with the private checkpoint

The model path below is deliberately redacted. Any checkpoint with the metadata
above should enter the same preparation path:

```bash
FLASHINFER_B12X_FORCE_MOE_W4A16=1 \
vllm serve <PRIVATE_QWEN3_6_35B_A3B_W4A16_CHECKPOINT> \
  --served-model-name qwen3_6_35b_nvfp4 \
  --port 8092 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video":0}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 3221225472 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_b12x \
  --compilation-config \
    '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8]}'
```

The failure is also reachable with eager execution, so it is not caused by CUDA
graph capture. B12x prepares the packed weights during the first forward/warmup.

### Public checkpoints with a matching structure

The closest public replacement is
[`kyaky/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/kyaky/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4).
It has the same Qwen3.6-35B-A3B architecture and 256 routed experts. Its model
card explicitly describes the same mixed quantization contract: FP8 attention,
GDN, and shared-expert paths; compressed-tensors NVFP4 weight-only W4A16 routed
experts; and BF16 output/router/vision components. Its published size is 22.5
GB, so it should exercise the same memory-constrained B12x preparation path.

```bash
FLASHINFER_B12X_FORCE_MOE_W4A16=1 \
vllm serve kyaky/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 \
  --port 8092 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 3221225472 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_b12x \
  --compilation-config \
    '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8]}'
```

I have not rerun the failure with this public checkpoint yet; it is provided as
a non-sensitive reproduction candidate with the same architecture, expert
count, model scale, W4A16 expert mode, and serialization path.

`Sehyo/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-NVFP4` and most other public llm-compressor NVFP4
checkpoints are not exact substitutes: their configs contain dynamic 4-bit
`input_activations`, making them W4A4 rather than the W4A16 path reported here.

[`nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4)
matches the Qwen3.6 architecture and model size more exactly, but it uses
ModelOpt serialization. It is useful for checking whether the lifetime problem
also affects the ModelOpt W4A16 input path, rather than as an exact replacement
for the compressed-tensors reproduction.

Current vLLM main also has a separate W4A16 propagation regression, tracked by
#43929. To isolate this memory issue, the B12x wrapper must receive
`quant_mode="w4a16"` and `source_format="compressed_tensors"` (or use a build
containing the equivalent propagation fix).

Observed during the first W4A16 preparation:

```text
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 768.00 MiB.
GPU 0 has a total capacity of 31.36 GiB with approximately 388 MiB free.
```

The immediate allocation came from `_nvfp4_compute_scale_factor()`, which
materialized a full FP32 scale copy and a boolean mask. Replacing that reduction
with a scalar `packed_scales.max()` removes this particular 768 MiB allocation,
but does not address the persistent duplicate packed expert weights.

## Expected behavior

B12x W4A16 preparation should have a bounded peak and should not retain both
complete source and kernel-packed expert layouts when only the packed layout is
needed for serving. Possible designs include:

- prepare in `process_weights_after_loading()` and replace/deregister the source
  expert parameters after correctness checks;
- load an offline-prepacked B12x checkpoint layout directly;
- stream conversion layer by layer before the entire source model is resident;
- make prepared weights layer-owned with an explicit lifecycle instead of an
  unbounded process-global pointer-keyed cache.

At minimum, the scale-factor reduction should avoid full-size FP32 and boolean
temporaries.

## Related work / duplicate check

- vllm-project/vllm#43929 fixes W4A16 routing and source-format propagation. It
  does not address repacking memory or packed-weight lifetime.
- vllm-project/vllm#44209 concerns KV-cache reservation and CUDA-graph capture
  OOM. This failure occurs earlier in B12x W4A16 weight preparation.
- flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3336 introduced/replaced the SM120 W4A16 preparation
  and dispatch path containing the global packed-weight cache; it does not
  address integration with a framework that already owns the source weights.
- vllm-project/vllm#37113 mentions experimental B12x runtime-state cleanup, but
  does not report or fix W4A16 source-plus-packed expert weight residency.

I searched both vLLM and FlashInfer issues/PRs for B12x W4A16 packed-weight OOM,
`_W4A16_WEIGHT_CACHE`, and `prepare_w4a16_packed_weights`; I did not find an
existing report for this specific persistent duplication and startup peak.

results.title: [ROCm][Perf] Cache static E8M0 weight-scale fp32 upcast in AITER FP8 block-scaled linear
results.body:
## Summary

DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP8 block-scaled GEMMs on ROCm call `_upcast_e8m0_to_fp32(Bs)` on every forward pass for the **static weight-scale** tensor `Bs`. On gfx942 this emits ~236 `aten::__lshift__` kernels per decode step (~1.0 ms/token at conc=1, 120k context) plus redundant `.contiguous()` copies. The upcast result is identical every step because `Bs` comes from checkpoint weights.

This PR memoizes the fp32 upcast keyed by `Bs.data_ptr()` (stable for the process lifetime and CUDA-graph safe). Dynamic activation scales (`As`) remain uncached.

In the mixed-dtype branch of `AiterFp8BlockScaledMMKernel.apply_block_scaled_mm`, E8M0 weight scales previously fell through to `Bs.to(torch.float32)`, which does not preserve E8M0 semantics. The cached path uses `_upcast_e8m0_to_fp32` instead.

**Scope:** ROCm + AITER FP8 block-scaled linear only. CUDA and other quantization paths are unchanged.

### gfx942 and gfx950 applicability

This change is **not gfx942-specific**. It applies on any ROCm CDNA path that selects `AiterFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` and still sees E8M0 weight scales (`Bs.dtype == torch.float8_e8m0fnu`) in the mixed-dtype forward branch -- including **gfx950** (MI355X) deployments using the same block-scaled FP8 / MXFP4 stack.

**Caveats:**

- Performance numbers below are **validated on MI325X (gfx942) only**; gfx950 impact is not yet measured.
- Upstream already upcasts E8M0 weight scales to fp32 in `process_weights_after_loading()` for many layers. Where that load-time path applies, static `Bs` may already be fp32 at forward time and this cache is belt-and-suspenders (still fixes incorrect `Bs.to(float32)` when E8M0 `Bs` does reach the mixed-dtype branch).
- Dynamic activation scales (`As`) are never cached.

## What changed

- `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/aiter.py`
  - Add module-level `_E8M0_WS_FP32_CACHE` and `_cached_upcast_e8m0_weight_scale()`
  - In `AiterFp8BlockScaledMMKernel.apply_block_scaled_mm`, route static E8M0 `Bs` through the cache; leave dynamic `As` uncached

## Selection & gating

- **Enabled when:** `AiterFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` is selected (ROCm, aiter installed, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, block-scaled FP8 config) and `Bs.dtype == torch.float8_e8m0fnu`
- **Fallback:** unchanged -- non-E8M0 scales still use `.to(torch.float32)`; non-ROCm / non-aiter backends unaffected
- **Env / config:** none (always on for the aiter block-scaled path)

## Depends on

None. Pure vLLM-side change; no aiter rebuild or new kernels.

## Related work

- Complements existing AITER FP8 block-scaled GEMM wiring on gfx942/gfx950; does not change GEMM kernel selection.
- Independent of sparse-attention / MoE perf PRs (e.g. #46275, #50470).

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `E8M0`, `weight_scale`, `block-scaled`, and `scaled_mm/aiter.py`; no open PR memoizes the E8M0 weight-scale upcast on this path.

Closest related work routes other ROCm FP8 paths through aiter but does not address per-step static-scale recomputation in `AiterFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`.

## Performance

**Environment:** 8x AMD Instinct MI325X (gfx942), TP8, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, 120k context, conc=1 decode profile  
**Method:** same optimized-stack image; baseline vs candidate differs only by this change  
**gfx950:** applicable in principle; step-level and E2E numbers below are gfx942-only until profiled on MI355X

### Step-level (decode)

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Decode step (ms/token) | 18.18 | 16.14 | **-11.2%** |
| GPU kernels / step | 2905 | 2433 | -472 |
| `__lshift__` launches / step | 236 | 0 | -236 |

### E2E serving (131k ISL)

| conc | median TPOT before -> after | Change TPOT |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 25.98 -> 24.2 ms | ~-6 to -7% |
| 8 | 29.37 -> 27.4 ms | ~-6 to -7% |

TTFT unchanged (decode-centric win).

## Accuracy

| Task | Metric | Baseline | Proposed |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K | flexible-extract (500 ex.) | 94.2% | 94.2% |

Identical by construction -- memoized pure function of a static parameter tensor.

## Test Plan

**Testing environment**

```text
Hardware: 8x MI325X (gfx942), TP8
Model:    deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
Server:   VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1, VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1,
          kv_cache_dtype=fp8_e4m3, max_model_len=131072
Baseline: upstream main
Candidate: upstream main + this PR
```

- Unit tests (cache hit/miss):

  ```bash
  python3 -m pytest -q tests/kernels/quantization/ -k "fp8 or block" --no-header
  ```

- Decode profile A/B (gfx942): confirm `__lshift__` kernel count -> 0 after warmup on DSv4 decode step
- Decode profile A/B (gfx950, pending): repeat kernel-count check on MI355X; expect benefit only if E8M0 `Bs` still hits the forward mixed-dtype branch

- Accuracy:

  ```bash
  lm_eval --model local-completions \
    --tasks gsm8k \
    --model_args "base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash" \
    --num_fewshot 5 --limit 500
  ```

- Pre-commit:

results.title: [Performance]: DeepEP v2 (ElasticBuffer) finalize_async runs combine synchronously — the shared-expert overlap window is never used
results.body:
### Report

`prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py` issues the DeepEP v2 (ElasticBuffer) combine **synchronously** at both call sites ([L171](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f179b57aa8ab6f634f508128ce1f1efadd0eb1/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py#L171), [L390](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f179b57aa8ab6f634f508128ce1f1efadd0eb1/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py#L390) pass `async_with_compute_stream=False`; the module docstring at [L45](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f179b57aa8ab6f634f508128ce1f1efadd0eb1/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py#L45) states both modes are synchronous).

The modular-kernel orchestration already supports overlapping **shared experts** with finalize (`finalize_async` -> shared experts on the compute stream -> receiver join, `MK_INTERNAL_OVERLAPPED`), but with a synchronous combine that window is fully occupied by the combine itself. For MoE models with a shared expert (DeepSeek-R1/V3), the shared-expert FFN therefore serializes behind the cross-node all-to-all on every MoE layer during decode.

### Prototype + evidence

We run DeepSeek-R1-671B (FP8) with `--all2all-backend deepep_v2` under full cudagraphs and prototyped a flag-gated change: combine issued with `async_with_compute_stream=True` (+ `allocate_on_comm_stream`), with `finalize_async` returning a receiver closure that waits the combine event on the compute stream (graph-replay safe). Observations on EP8 (2 nodes x 4 GPUs, TP4xDP2, GB300 / multi-node NVLink):

- **Pre-registered A/B** (4 independent server starts in ABBA order; greedy, forced 128 output tokens; steady-state ITL after warmup): **ITL p50 -8.8% @C=1 (15.71 -> 14.32 ms), -5.3% @C=24**; p99 improves similarly (no tail regression). TTFT unchanged (-0.1 ms), as expected for a decode-only change (negative control).
- **Correctness**: greedy outputs bit-identical across all four arms (same text hash). Kernel-level: 300 varied-input replays bitwise-equal vs the sync reference, both eager and inside a captured graph.
- **Serving traces**: with the flag ON, each combine kernel is overlapped by shared-expert GEMMs for ~9.7 us on average (~22% of combine busy time, consistent across ranks); with it OFF the measured overlap is exactly 0.
- **Ablation**: async combine with the event-wait placed *before* the shared-expert GEMMs (offload without overlap) shows ~0 gain - the benefit is true overlap, not stream offload. The per-layer benefit grows with EP size (~13 us/layer @EP4 -> ~18 us/layer @EP32 in isolated microbenchmarks).

### Question

Is there maintainer interest in a PR enabling this (initially env-gated, default off, disabled under DBO)? Happy to submit with a CPU contract test plus a bitwise oracle added to the DeepEP v2 GPU test, and to adapt the shape (e.g. always-on) per your guidance.

results.title: [Kernel][MoE] DeepEP v2: async finalize to overlap shared experts with combine
results.body:
> **Status (2026-08-31):** reviewer feedback addressed — overlap is now **default-on** (`VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_COMBINE_OVERLAP=1`, capability-gated fallback, env is a kill-switch), rebased clean onto current main (no conflicts). **Blocked only on a `ready` label** so Buildkite can run — the full suite has never executed on this fork PR. Contract tests included; EP8 A/B in comments.

---

FIX #52744

### What

`prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py` issues the ElasticBuffer combine synchronously at both call sites, so the modular-kernel shared-expert overlap window (`finalize_async` -> shared experts on the compute stream -> receiver join, `MK_INTERNAL_OVERLAPPED`) is never used: for MoE models with a shared expert (DeepSeek-R1/V3) the shared-expert FFN serializes behind the cross-node all-to-all on every MoE layer during decode.

This PR makes `finalize_async` issue the combine with `async_with_compute_stream=True` (+ `allocate_on_comm_stream`) and return a receiver closure that joins via a device-side `event.current_stream_wait()` — graph-replay safe (the closure keeps `combined_x` and the event alive; no host synchronization inside the captured region).

### Safety

- **On by default** (per review feedback): `VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_COMBINE_OVERLAP=0` forces the synchronous combine. The flag is read once in `__init__` (never touches `os.environ` inside the captured region). Output is byte-identical either way.
- **DBO**: overlap is disabled under DBO (`dbo_enabled()`), synchronous fallback, log-once.
- **No-event capability gate**: if a DeepEP build returns no combine event, the overlap self-disables permanently (warn-once + a single eager full-sync join) — a pre-capture decision, since warmup always precedes capture; if it is ever hit during capture anyway, a hard `RuntimeError` is raised instead of hiding a sync inside the graph.

### Tests

- `tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_overlap_gate.py` (new, hermetic, no GPU collectives): contract tests for the gate — eager no-event self-disable / capture no-event raise / event-path deferred device-side join. (Ported from a validated harness; the same three contracts pass against this module logic.)
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py`: `test_deep_ep_v2_moe_backends` parametrized over the flag, so the existing torch-reference comparison doubles as the correctness oracle with overlap ON, across eager/cudagraph and both experts backends. That test's MoE has no shared expert, so it also covers the degenerate "async combine with nothing to overlap" path.

### Performance (deployment observation)

DeepSeek-R1-671B FP8, EP8 (2 nodes x TP4xDP2, GB300 / multi-node NVLink), full cudagraphs, `--all2all-backend deepep_v2`; pre-registered A/B, 4 independent server starts (ABBA), greedy, forced 128 output tokens, steady-state:

| metric | OFF | ON | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| C=1 decode ITL p50 | 15.71 ms | 14.32 ms | **-8.8%** |
| C=24 decode ITL p50 | 22.05 ms | 20.89 ms | **-5.3%** |
| C=1 TTFT p50 (negative control) | 236.9 ms | 236.8 ms | -0.1 ms |

Greedy outputs bit-identical across all four arms. Serving traces: each combine kernel overlapped by shared-expert GEMMs ~9.7 us on average with the flag ON vs exactly 0 OFF. An ablation with the event-wait placed *before* the shared-expert GEMMs (offload without overlap) shows ~0 gain — the benefit is true overlap. Full evidence in #52744.

### Validation scope

GPU validation was performed on a v0.26.0-era tree; the finalize/combine region is unchanged between v0.26.0 and current main (the dispatch-side drift is unrelated), so the port is mechanical. The contract tests pass against this module logic; the parametrized cudagraph test covers the captured path wherever DeepEP v2 CI runners exist. Default flipped to on per review feedback; the env var remains as an escape hatch.
